Side Lanes & Split Pushing

After laning ends, games are won by who controls the side lanes. Learn who should be where, how to split push without throwing, and how to run a 1-3-1.

Why side lanes decide mid games

Once the outer turrets start falling, most players do the same thing: everybody walks to mid and stands around as a group of five. It feels safe, but it wastes gold. Minion waves keep spawning in top and bot lane, and from 14:00 they come every 25 seconds (every 20 seconds after 30:00). Every wave you ignore is gold and experience that slowly pushes into your own turret.

Side lane control means always having the right person catching those waves, so your team keeps earning while still being able to group for an objective. The team that handles side lanes well usually has an item lead by 25 minutes without winning a single big fight.

It also creates pressure. A wave crashing into an enemy turret has to be answered. If the enemy sends someone to clear it, they are now four players against your five near Dragon or Baron.

Who should be where

A simple default for the mid game:

  • Top side lane: your best duelist or the champion with Teleport. That's usually your Top Lane laner.
  • Bot side lane: the lane closest to the next objective gets the group. If Dragon is up soon, your team groups bot side and the solo player goes top.
  • Mid lane: your mid laner or ADC, someone who can clear a wave fast from a safe distance.
  • Jungle and support: they move between lanes with vision, and are the first to arrive at an objective.

The ADC should not farm a side lane alone without vision in the mid game. Marksmen die instantly to a single gank, and a dead ADC near Baron time often loses the game. Let your ADC farm the side lane closest to your team, or the mid lane.

Common mistakeSending your squishy ADC into the far side lane while the enemy jungler is missing. If you can't see at least three enemies on the map, the side lane is the most dangerous place to stand.

How to split push safely

Split pushing means one player pushes a side lane deep while the team stays elsewhere. Done well, it forces two enemies to come answer, which gives your team a 4v3 somewhere else. Done badly, it's just a free kill.

Before you split, check three things:

  1. Can you win a 1v1 against whoever will come? Champions like Fiora, Jax, Tryndamere and Yorick are built for this. Items like Hullbreaker make you even better at it.
  2. Where are the enemies? If you see four on the other side of the map, push freely. If you see two or fewer, back off toward your own side of the river.
  3. Is there vision? Ward the enemy jungle entrances near your lane. A ward on the Faelight near the side lane gives you a much wider view for 45 seconds.

Turrets are easier to hit now than in past years. Crystalline Overgrowth grows on lane turrets after 1:30, and your next champion attack on that turret pops the crystal for bonus true damage. Melee champions also deal 20% more damage to turrets. Runes like Demolish and the three Void Grubs (their buff spawns Voidmites while you hit structures) make a split pusher very scary.

Pro tipPush the wave in before you start hitting the turret. Turrets target minions first, so a full wave under the turret is free damage for you.

The 1-3-1 formation

A 1-3-1 means one player in top lane, three in mid, and one in bot lane. It's the strongest setup in the mid game when you have two good side laners, because the enemy can't group five without giving up two lanes.

It works because of a simple rule: you never fight five against five. If the enemy groups on your top laner, your mid three push a turret. If they group mid, both side laners hit turrets. If they split up, your three in mid fight their smaller group.

For a 1-3-1 you need:

  • Two players who can survive alone or escape (Teleport, dashes, or just strong 1v1s).
  • A mid group that can clear waves and isn't easily dived. Long-range mages like Xerath or Ziggs are great here.
  • Deep vision in both enemy jungle halves so the side laners see collapses coming.

Crossmapping and Teleport plays

Crossmapping means trading objectives on opposite sides of the map. If the enemy starts Dragon and you can't contest it, don't walk into a losing fight. Instead, take something of similar value on the other side: a turret with plates, the Rift Herald, or Baron if they're far away.

Plates matter more in 2026 because they no longer fall off at 14:00. Outer, inner and inhibitor turrets all have five plates for the whole game, so a crossmap turret is often worth almost as much as a drake.

Teleport makes all of this possible. Your top laner gets Unleashed Teleport for free from their role quest. It has a long cooldown (390 seconds), so it's a big decision each time. Good uses:

  • Teleporting to a ward behind the enemy team as a fight starts at Dragon.
  • Teleporting to a side lane to stop a split pusher, then back to the group later.
  • Pushing your side wave first, then teleporting, so you don't lose the wave for nothing.
Pro tipTell your team your Teleport timer. A top laner with Teleport up is a fifth player at every fight; without it, your team should play more carefully around objectives.

When to stop splitting and group

Split pushing is a tool, not a lifestyle. Group up when:

  • Baron, Elder Dragon or the fourth drake is about to spawn. Your team needs you.
  • The enemy has a strong group fighter and your team can't hold 4v5.
  • You just died, or the enemy team has three or more members missing near your lane.
  • Your team has a big item lead and can simply force a 5v5.

The worst thing is to be halfway: not pushing deep enough to pull enemies, and too far to help the fight. Make a decision. Either commit to the side lane and keep pushing, or walk to your team early.

Key takeaways

  • Never leave side waves uncaught. Minion waves come every 25s after 14:00 and are free gold.
  • Send your best duelist (often the top laner with Unleashed Teleport) to the far side lane; keep the ADC near the team.
  • Only split when you can see where the enemies are and you can beat whoever comes.
  • A 1-3-1 forces the enemy to choose what to give up, and avoids 5v5 fights.
  • If you can't contest an objective, crossmap: plates never fall off now, so turrets stay valuable.
